questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Two charged spherical conductors of radius $R_1$ and $R_2$ are connected by a wire. Then the ratio of surface charge densities of the spheres $(\sigma_1 / \sigma_2)$ is:
questions.explanation: When connected, potentials equalize: $V_1 = V_2 \implies \frac{Q_1}{R_1} = \frac{Q_2}{R_2}$. Since $\sigma = \frac{Q}{4\pi R^2}$, ratio $\frac{\sigma_1}{\sigma_2} = \frac{Q_1 / R_1^2}{Q_2 / R_2^2} = \frac{R_2}{R_1}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The velocity of a small ball of mass $M$ and density $d$, when dropped in a container filled with glycerine becomes constant after some time. If density of glycerine is $d/2$, then the viscous force acting on the ball is:
questions.explanation: At terminal velocity, $F_v + F_B = Mg \implies F_v + \left(\frac{d/2}{d}\right)Mg = Mg \implies F_v = \frac{Mg}{2}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: An infinitely long straight conductor carries a current of $5\text{ A}$. An electron is moving with speed $10^5\text{ m/s}$ parallel to the conductor at a distance $20\text{ cm}$. Magnitude of magnetic force on electron is:
questions.explanation: $B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r} = \frac{4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times 5}{2\pi \times 0.2} = 5 \times 10^{-6}\text{ T}$. Force $F = q v B = (1.6 \times 10^{-19}) \times 10^5 \times (5 \times 10^{-6}) = 8 \times 10^{-20}\text{ N}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A dipole is placed in a non-uniform electric field as shown. In which direction will it move?
questions.optionA: Towards the left as its potential energy will increase
questions.optionB: Towards the right as its potential energy will decrease
questions.optionC: Towards the left as its potential energy will decrease
questions.optionD: Towards the right as its potential energy will increase
questions.explanation: Field is stronger to the right (lines converge). Force on $+q$ to the right exceeds force on $-q$ to the left. Dipole moves right towards minimum potential energy.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A lens of large focal length and large aperture is best suited as an objective of an astronomical telescope since:
questions.optionA: A large aperture contributes to the quality and visibility of images
questions.optionB: A large area of objective ensures better light gathering power
questions.optionC: A large aperture provides better resolution
questions.explanation: Large aperture maximizes light gathering power, reduces diffraction for higher resolving power, and improves image clarity.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A screw gauge has main scale reading $0\text{ mm}$ and circular scale reading 52 divisions. If $1\text{ mm}$ on main scale corresponds to 100 circular divisions, diameter of wire is:
questions.explanation: Least Count $= \frac{1\text{ mm}}{100} = 0.01\text{ mm} = 0.001\text{ cm}$. Diameter $= 0 + 52 \times 0.001\text{ cm} = 0.052\text{ cm}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A nucleus with mass number 240 (BE/A $= 7.6\text{ MeV}$) breaks into two fragments of mass 120 each (BE/A $= 8.5\text{ MeV}$). Total gain in Binding Energy is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A small block slides down a smooth inclined plane from rest at $t=0$. If $S_n$ is distance travelled in interval $t=n-1$ to $t=n$, then ratio $S_n / S_{n+1}$ is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Find the angle of emergence from a prism of refractive index $\sqrt{3}$ with incident ray perpendicular to first face ($A = 60^\circ$):
questions.explanation: At first face, $r_1 = 0^\circ \implies r_2 = A - r_1 = 60^\circ$. At second face, $\sin e = \mu \sin r_2 = \sqrt{3} \sin 30^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \implies e = 60^\circ$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A spring is stretched by $5\text{ cm}$ by force $10\text{ N}$. Time period of oscillations when mass of $2\text{ kg}$ is suspended is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Convex lens A ($f=20\text{ cm}$) and concave lens B ($f=5\text{ cm}$) are coaxial separated by distance $d$. If parallel beam leaves B parallel, distance $d$ is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText:
Match Column-I with Column-II:
Column-I: (A) Drift Velocity, (B) Electrical Resistivity, (C) Relaxation Period, (D) Current Density
Column-II: (P) $m / (n e^2 \rho)$, (Q) $n e v_d$, (R) $e E \tau / m$, (S) $E / J$
Choose the correct option:
questions.explanation: Drift velocity $v_d = eE\tau/m$, Resistivity $\rho = E/J$, Relaxation time $\tau = m/(ne^2\rho)$, Current density $J = nev_d$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Electron concentration in n-type equals hole concentration in p-type. When equal electric field is applied, current comparison is:
questions.optionA: Current in n-type = current in p-type
questions.optionB: Current in p-type > current in n-type
questions.optionC: Current in n-type > current in p-type
questions.explanation: Electron mobility $\mu_e$ is higher than hole mobility $\mu_h \implies I_n > I_p$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A radioactive nucleus undergoes decay: $^A_Z X \to _{Z-1} B \to _{Z-3} C \to _{Z-2} D$. The decay particles in sequence are:
questions.explanation: $Z \to Z-1$ ($ eta^+$ emission), $Z-1 \to Z-3$ ($alpha$ emission), $Z-3 \to Z-2$ ($ eta^-$ emission).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Water falls from height $60\text{ m}$ at rate $15\text{ kg/s}$ on a turbine. If frictional losses are $10\%$, power generated is ($g=10\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.explanation: $P_{\text{in}} = \frac{mgh}{t} = 15 \times 10 \times 60 = 9000\text{ W} = 9\text{ kW}$. Efficiency $= 90\% \implies P = 0.9 \times 9 = 8.1\text{ kW}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Number of photons per second emitted by monochromatic source ($600\text{ nm}$) delivering power $3.3 \times 10^{-3}\text{ W}$ is:
questions.explanation: $n = \frac{P \lambda}{hc} = \frac{(3.3 \times 10^{-3}) \times (600 \times 10^{-9})}{(6.6 \times 10^{-34}) \times (3 \times 10^8)} = 10^{16}\text{ photons/s}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: For a plane EM wave propagating in $+x$-direction, possible directions for $\vec{E}$ and $\vec{B}$ are:
questions.explanation: $\vec{E} \times \vec{B}$ must point along $+\hat{i}$. $(-\hat{j}+\hat{k}) \times (-\hat{j}-\hat{k}) = 2\hat{i}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Parallel combination of 4 identical wires has resistance $0.25\,\Omega$. If connected in series, effective resistance is:
questions.explanation: $R_p = R/4 = 0.25 \implies R = 1\,\Omega$. In series: $R_s = 4R = 4\,\Omega$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A cell of EMF $1.5\text{ V}$ gives balance point at $36\text{ cm}$. Another cell of EMF $2.5\text{ V}$ gives balance point at:
questions.explanation: $\frac{E_1}{E_2} = \frac{l_1}{l_2} \implies \frac{1.5}{2.5} = \frac{36}{l_2} \implies l_2 = 60\text{ cm}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Polar molecules are the molecules:
questions.optionB: Acquiring dipole moment only in electric field
questions.optionC: Acquiring dipole moment only in absence of magnetic field
questions.optionD: Having a permanent electric dipole moment
questions.explanation: In polar molecules, centers of positive and negative charges do not coincide, giving permanent dipole moments.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A parallel plate capacitor has electric field $E$, plate separation $d$, and area $A$. Energy stored in capacitor is:
questions.explanation: $U = u \times \text{Volume} = \frac{1}{2} \varepsilon_0 E^2 (A d)$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: The equivalent capacitance of the combination of 3 capacitors of capacitance $C$ shown in figure is:
questions.explanation: Middle capacitor is shorted; top and bottom capacitors are in parallel $\implies C_{\text{eq}} = 2C$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText:
Consider statements:
(A) A zener diode is connected in reverse bias as voltage regulator.
(B) Potential barrier of p-n junction lies between $0.1\text{ V}$ to $0.3\text{ V}$.
Choose correct answer:
questions.explanation: (A) is correct. (B) is incorrect because potential barrier for Si is $\sim 0.7\text{ V}$ and Ge is $\sim 0.3\text{ V}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A particle is dropped from height $S$. At a certain height, $\text{KE} = 3\,\text{PE}$. The height from ground and speed at that instant are:
questions.explanation: $\text{PE} = mg h$, $\text{KE} = mg(S-h) = 3mgh \implies h = S/4$. Speed $v = \sqrt{2g(3S/4)} = \sqrt{\frac{3gS}{2}}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: If $E$ and $G$ denote energy and gravitational constant, dimensions of $E/G$ are:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText:
Match Column-I with Column-II (Kinetic Theory):
(A) RMS speed, (B) Pressure of ideal gas, (C) Average KE of a molecule, (D) Total internal energy of 1 mole diatomic gas
(P) $\frac{1}{3} n m \bar{v}^2$, (Q) $\sqrt{\frac{3RT}{M}}$, (R) $\frac{5}{2} RT$, (S) $\frac{3}{2} k_B T$
Choose the correct option:
questions.explanation: $v_{\text{rms}} = \sqrt{3RT/M}$ (Q), $P = \frac{1}{3}nm\bar{v}^2$ (P), $KE_{\text{molecule}} = \frac{3}{2}k_B T$ (S), $U_{\text{diatomic}} = \frac{5}{2}RT$ (R).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A body executes SHM with frequency $n$. The frequency of its potential energy oscillations is:
questions.explanation: $U = \frac{1}{2} k A^2 \sin^2(\omega t) = \frac{1}{4} k A^2 (1 - \cos 2\omega t) \implies$ frequency is $2n$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Coffee cools from $90^\circ\text{C}$ to $80^\circ\text{C}$ in $t\text{ min}$ (room temp $20^\circ\text{C}$). Time taken to cool from $80^\circ\text{C}$ to $60^\circ\text{C}$ is:
questions.explanation: Newton's law: $\frac{10}{t} = K(65) \implies K = \frac{2}{13t}$. For second cooling: $\frac{20}{t'} = K(50) = \frac{2}{13t}(50) \implies t' = \frac{13}{5}t$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A capacitor $C$ is connected across $V = V_0 \sin\omega t$. Displacement current $I_d$ is:
questions.explanation: $q = C V_0 \sin\omega t \implies I_d = \frac{dq}{dt} = V_0 \omega C \cos\omega t$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Half-life of nuclide is $100\text{ hours}$. Fraction of original activity remaining after $150\text{ hours}$ is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Series LCR circuit has $V_L = 40\text{ V}, V_C = 10\text{ V}, V_R = 40\text{ V}$. Amplitude of current is $10\sqrt{2}\text{ A}$. Impedance $Z$ is:
questions.explanation: $V_{\text{rms}} = \sqrt{V_R^2 + (V_L - V_C)^2} = \sqrt{40^2 + 30^2} = 50\text{ V}$. $I_{\text{rms}} = \frac{10\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}} = 10\text{ A} \implies Z = \frac{50}{10} = 5\,\Omega$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Thick cable of radius $R$ carries current $I$ uniformly distributed. The variation of $B(r)$ with distance $r$ from axis is:
questions.optionC: Linearly increasing for $r \le R$, then decreasing as $1/r$ for $r > R$
questions.explanation: $B = \frac{\mu_0 I r}{2\pi R^2}$ inside ($r \le R$) and $B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r}$ outside ($r > R$).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Electromagnetic wave of wavelength $\lambda$ emits photoelectrons of de-Broglie wavelength $\lambda_d$. Neglecting work function, $\lambda$ is:
questions.explanation: $E = \frac{hc}{\lambda} = \frac{p^2}{2m} = \frac{h^2}{2m \lambda_d^2} \implies \lambda = \left(\frac{2mc}{h}\right) \lambda_d^2$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Escape velocity from Earth is $v$. Escape velocity from planet with radius $4R$ and same density is:
questions.explanation: $v_e = R \sqrt{\frac{8\pi G \rho}{3}} \propto R \implies v' = 4v$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: If Force $[F]$, acceleration $[A]$ and time $[T]$ are fundamental quantities, dimensions of Energy are:
questions.explanation: $\text{Energy} = \text{Force} \times \text{Displacement} = [F] \times [\frac{1}{2} A T^2] = [F][A][T^2]$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Two concentric coplanar circular loops have radii $R_1 \gg R_2$. Mutual inductance $M$ is directly proportional to:
questions.explanation: $M = \frac{\mu_0 \pi R_2^2}{2 R_1} \propto \frac{R_2^2}{R_1}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Point object is $60\text{ cm}$ from convex lens ($f=30\text{ cm}$). A plane mirror is placed $40\text{ cm}$ behind lens. Final image is at:
questions.explanation: Lens forms real image at $60\text{ cm}$ behind lens ($20\text{ cm}$ behind mirror). Mirror reflects light to form real image $20\text{ cm}$ in front of mirror.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Three resistors $r_1, r_2, r_3$ are connected with $r_2, r_3$ in parallel. The ratio $i_3 / i_1$ is:
questions.explanation: By current division in parallel branches: $i_3 = i_1 \left(\frac{r_2}{r_2 + r_3}\right) \implies \frac{i_3}{i_1} = \frac{r_2}{r_2+r_3}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: For digital inputs A, B, C applied to logic circuit (AND gates fed into OR gate), output $y$ is:
questions.explanation: Circuit implements $y = (A \cdot B) + (B \cdot C)$. Evaluation of interval logic levels matches waveform (3).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Series LCR has $L=5.0\text{ H}, C=80\,\mu\text{F}, R=40\,\Omega$. Frequencies where power is half maximum (half-power frequencies) are:
questions.explanation: $\omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}} = 50\text{ rad/s}$. $\Delta\omega = \frac{R}{2L} = \frac{40}{10} = 4\text{ rad/s} \implies \omega = 50 \pm 4 = 46\text{ rad/s}$ and $54\text{ rad/s}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Car accelerates at $5\text{ m/s}^2$. At $t=4\text{ s}$, ball is dropped. Velocity and acceleration of ball at $t=6\text{ s}$ are:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Particle projected with velocity $v = k V_e$ ($k < 1$). Maximum height reached above Earth surface is:
questions.explanation: Conservation of energy: $-\frac{GMm}{R} + \frac{1}{2} m (k^2 \frac{2GM}{R}) = -\frac{GMm}{R+h} \implies h = \frac{R k^2}{1 - k^2}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Particle in circle radius $R$ takes period $T$. If projected at angle $\theta$, maximum height is $4R$. Angle $\theta$ is:
questions.explanation: $v = \frac{2\pi R}{T}$. $H = \frac{v^2 \sin^2\theta}{2g} = 4R \implies \sin\theta = \left(\frac{2gT^2}{\pi^2 R}\right)^{1/2}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Given $\vec{F} = q(\vec{v} \times \vec{B})$ where $q=1, \vec{v} = 2\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+6\hat{k}$ and $\vec{F} = 4\hat{i}-20\hat{j}+12\hat{k}$. Vector $\vec{B}$ is:
questions.explanation: Cross product of $(2\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+6\hat{k}) \times (-6\hat{i}-6\hat{j}-8\hat{k})$ gives $4\hat{i}-20\hat{j}+12\hat{k}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A ball of mass $0.15\text{ kg}$ is dropped from $10\text{ m}$ and rebounds to same height. Magnitude of impulse is ($g=10\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.explanation: $v = \sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{200} = 14.14\text{ m/s}$. Impulse $= m(v - (-v)) = 2 m v = 2(0.15)(14.14) \approx 4.2\text{ N s}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Wire of length $12a$ wound into (i) equilateral triangle of side $a$ (4 turns), (ii) square of side $a$ (3 turns). Ratio of magnetic moments is:
questions.explanation: $M_1 = 4 \times I \times (\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} a^2) = \sqrt{3} I a^2$. $M_2 = 3 \times I \times a^2 = 3 I a^2$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: Twenty seven drops charged to $220\text{ V}$ each combine to form bigger drop. Potential of bigger drop is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A uniform rod of length $200\text{ cm}$, mass $500\text{ g}$ balanced on wedge at $40\text{ cm}$. Mass $2\text{ kg}$ suspended at $20\text{ cm}$ and unknown $m$ at $160\text{ cm}$. Mass $m$ is:
questions.explanation: Torque about wedge: $2(20) = 0.5(60) + m(120) \implies 40 = 30 + 120m \implies m = 10/120 = 1/12\text{ kg}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: From a circular ring of mass $M$, radius $R$, an arc of $90^\circ$ is removed. Moment of inertia of remaining part is $K M R^2$. Value of $K$ is:
questions.explanation: Mass remaining $= \frac{3}{4}M$. Distance of all points is $R \implies I = (3/4 M) R^2 \implies K = 3/4$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.questionText: A step-down transformer on $220\text{ V}$ operates an $11\text{ V}, 44\text{ W}$ lamp. Current in primary circuit is:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Dihedral angle of least stable conformer (eclipsed) of ethane is:
questions.explanation: In eclipsed conformation of ethane, dihedral angle between C-H bonds is $0^\circ$, causing maximum torsional strain.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Noble gases are inert. Identify an INCORRECT statement about them:
questions.optionA: Noble gases are sparingly soluble in water
questions.optionB: Noble gases have very high melting and boiling points
questions.optionC: Noble gases have weak dispersion forces
questions.optionD: Noble gases have large positive values of electron gain enthalpy
questions.explanation: Due to weak London dispersion forces, noble gases have extremely low melting and boiling points (Helium has lowest b.p. of $4.2\text{ K}$).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Major product of reaction: $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2 + \text{HBr} \xrightarrow{(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CO})_2\text{O}_2} \text{Product}$ is:
questions.explanation: Anti-Markovnikov addition via peroxide effect adds Br radical to terminal carbon, giving 1-bromo-3-methylbutane.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: A radio station broadcasts on frequency $1368\text{ kHz}$. Wavelength of EM radiation is ($c = 3.0 \times 10^8\text{ m/s}$):
questions.explanation: $\lambda = \frac{c}{\nu} = \frac{3.0 \times 10^8}{1368 \times 10^3} = 219.3\text{ m}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The INCORRECT statement among the following is:
questions.optionA: Actinoid contraction is greater than lanthanoid contraction
questions.optionB: Most of the trivalent Lanthanoid ions are colorless in solid state
questions.optionC: Lanthanoids are good conductors of heat and electricity
questions.optionD: Actinoids are highly reactive metals, especially when finely divided
questions.explanation: Many trivalent lanthanoid ions are coloured due to $f$-$f$ electronic transitions (e.g. $\text{Pr}^{3+}$ green, $\text{Nd}^{3+}$ pink).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Number of tetrahedral and octahedral voids in hexagonal primitive unit cell (hcp) are:
questions.explanation: For hcp ($Z = 6$), number of octahedral voids $= Z = 6$ and tetrahedral voids $= 2Z = 12$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Identify the compound that reacts with Hinsberg's reagent to give a solid which dissolves in alkali:
questions.explanation: Primary amines form N-alkylbenzenesulphonamide containing an acidic hydrogen on nitrogen, dissolving in alkali.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which of the following is a metal displacement redox reaction?
questions.explanation: Aluminium displaces chromium from its oxide (Thermite reduction).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Statement I: Aspirin and Paracetamol belong to narcotic analgesics.
Statement II: Morphine and Heroin are non-narcotic analgesics.
Choose correct option:
questions.optionA: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
questions.optionB: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.optionC: Statement I is correct but Statement II is false
questions.optionD: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true
questions.explanation: Aspirin and paracetamol are non-narcotic; morphine and heroin are habit-forming narcotic analgesics.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: IUPAC name of product formed in reaction: $\text{Acetone} + \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{MgBr} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+} \text{Product}$ is:
questions.explanation: Addition of ethyl Grignard to acetone gives 2-methylbutan-2-ol ($3^\circ$ alcohol).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Statement I: Acid strength increases as $\text{HF} \ll \text{HCl} \ll \text{HBr} \ll \text{HI}$.
Statement II: As halogen size increases down the group, $\text{H-X}$ bond strength decreases and acid strength increases.
Choose correct option:
questions.optionA: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
questions.optionB: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.optionC: Statement I is correct but Statement II is false
questions.optionD: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct; decreasing H-X bond dissociation enthalpy down the group dictates acidity.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Right relationship between $C_P$ and $C_V$ for one mole of ideal gas is:
questions.explanation: Mayer's formula: $C_P - C_V = R$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match List-I with List-II (Molecular Geometry):
List-I: (a) $\text{PCl}_5$, (b) $\text{SF}_6$, (c) $\text{BrF}_5$, (d) $\text{BF}_3$
List-II: (i) Square pyramidal, (ii) Trigonal planar, (iii) Octahedral, (iv) Trigonal bipyramidal
Choose the correct option:
questions.explanation: $\text{PCl}_5$ = TBP (iv), $\text{SF}_6$ = Octahedral (iii), $\text{BrF}_5$ = Square pyramidal (i), $\text{BF}_3$ = Trigonal planar (ii).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Solutions of $10\text{ g}$ glucose in $250\text{ mL}$ ($P_1$), $10\text{ g}$ urea in $250\text{ mL}$ ($P_2$), and $10\text{ g}$ sucrose in $250\text{ mL}$ ($P_3$). Decreasing order of osmotic pressure is:
questions.explanation: Osmotic pressure $\pi \propto n = w/M$. Molar masses: Urea (60) < Glucose (180) < Sucrose (342) $\implies P_2 > P_1 > P_3$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which method is used to obtain highly pure metal which is liquid at room temperature (Mercury)?
questions.explanation: Low boiling metals like Mercury and Zinc are refined by fractional distillation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Tritium, a radioactive isotope of hydrogen, emits which of the following particles?
questions.explanation: $^3_1\text{H} \to ^3_2\text{He} + \beta^- + \bar{\nu}$ (low energy $\beta^-$ emission, $t_{1/2} = 12.33\text{ years}$).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Number of body-centred unit cells among all 14 Bravais lattices is:
questions.explanation: Body-centred lattices exist in 3 crystal systems: Cubic, Tetragonal, and Orthorhombic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The major product formed in dehydrohalogenation of 2-bromopentane is pent-2-ene based on:
questions.explanation: Saytzeff's rule states that the more substituted, more stable alkene is the major elimination product.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The maximum temperature achieved in the combustion zone of a blast furnace is:
questions.explanation: In combustion zone near the tuyeres, coke combustion achieves temperatures up to $2200\text{ K}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Molar conductivities at infinite dilution: $\Lambda^\circ_{\text{NaCl}} = 126.45$, $\Lambda^\circ_{\text{HCl}} = 426.16$, $\Lambda^\circ_{\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}} = 91.0\text{ S cm}^2\text{mol}^{-1}$. $\Lambda^\circ_{\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}}$ is:
questions.explanation: Kohlrausch Law: $\Lambda^\circ = 426.16 + 91.0 - 126.45 = 390.71\text{ S cm}^2\text{mol}^{-1}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Ethylenediaminetetraacetate $(\text{EDTA})^{4-}$ ion is a:
questions.optionA: Hexadentate ligand with four 'O' and two 'N' donor atoms
questions.optionC: Bidentate ligand with two 'N' donor atoms
questions.explanation: EDTA is a hexadentate chelating ligand donating via 2 amino nitrogens and 4 carboxylate oxygens.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The structures of beryllium chloride ($\text{BeCl}_2$) in solid state and vapour phase are:
questions.explanation: In solid state, $\text{BeCl}_2$ forms polymeric chains with chloride bridges. In vapour at $<1200\text{ K}$, it is dimeric $(\text{BeCl}_2)_2$, becoming linear monomer at $>1200\text{ K}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The correct structure of 2,6-dimethyldec-4-ene has 10 carbons in principal chain with double bond at C4:
questions.optionA: 10-carbon chain with methyls at C2 and C6 and trans double bond at C4
questions.optionB: 8-carbon chain with double bond at C2
questions.explanation: 2,6-dimethyldec-4-ene has a 10-carbon main chain with double bond between carbons 4 and 5 and methyls at C2 and C6.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Tyndall effect is exhibited by which of the following?
questions.explanation: Tyndall scattering is shown by colloidal solutions (starch sol) where particle size matches light wavelength.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which one of the following polymers is prepared by addition polymerisation?
questions.explanation: Teflon is synthesized by chain-growth addition polymerisation of tetrafluoroethene ($n\,\text{CF}_2=\text{CF}_2$).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: RBC deficiency (Pernicious Anaemia) is caused by deficiency of:
questions.explanation: Vitamin $\text{B}_{12}$ deficiency impairs RBC maturation and leads to pernicious anaemia.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The correct decreasing sequence of bond enthalpy of 'C-X' bond is:
questions.explanation: As halogen size increases, orbital overlap decreases and bond enthalpy decreases: $\text{C-F} (452) > \text{C-Cl} (351) > \text{C-Br} (293) > \text{C-I} (234\text{ kJ/mol})$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: An organic compound contains $78\%$ carbon and $22\%$ hydrogen by weight. Empirical formula is:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Among the following alkaline earth metal halides, the one which is covalent and soluble in organic solvents is:
questions.explanation: Due to small size and high polarizing power of $\text{Be}^{2+}$ (Fajan's rule), $\text{BeCl}_2$ is predominantly covalent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: $\text{BF}_3$ is planar and electron deficient. Hybridization and valence electrons around boron are:
questions.explanation: Boron forms 3 sigma bonds with $sp^2$ trigonal planar geometry and has an incomplete octet (6 valence electrons).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: $pK_b$ of dimethylamine is 3.27 and $pK_a$ of acetic acid is 4.77. pH of dimethylammonium acetate solution is:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Boyle's law isotherms ($P$ vs $V$) at different temperatures show:
questions.optionA: Higher temperature isotherms lie higher up (further from origin)
questions.explanation: At a given volume, $P \propto T$. The isotherm for higher temperature ($600\text{ K}$) lies above $400\text{ K}$ and $200\text{ K}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: For reaction $\text{A} \to \text{B}$, $\Delta H = -4.2\text{ kJ/mol}$ and $E_a = 9.6\text{ kJ/mol}$. Potential energy profile shows:
questions.optionA: Exothermic profile with product energy lower than reactant by $4.2\text{ kJ/mol}$ and barrier of $9.6\text{ kJ/mol}$
questions.explanation: Exothermic reaction has products at lower potential energy than reactants with forward activation barrier $E_a$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which of the following molecular formulas can exhibit metamerism?
questions.explanation: $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$ forms metamers: $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5-\text{O}-\text{C}_2\text{H}_5$ (diethyl ether) and $\text{CH}_3-\text{O}-\text{C}_3\text{H}_7$ (methyl propyl ether).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: $\text{Zr}$ ($Z=40$) and $\text{Hf}$ ($Z=72$) have almost identical atomic and ionic radii because of:
questions.explanation: Lanthanoid contraction fills 14 electrons in poorly shielding $4f$ subshell, neutralizing the expected size increase.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match List-I with List-II (Spin-only Magnetic Moments):
(a) $[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]^{3-}$, (b) $[\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$, (c) $[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]^{4-}$, (d) $[\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$
(i) $5.92\text{ BM}$, (ii) $0\text{ BM}$, (iii) $4.90\text{ BM}$, (iv) $1.73\text{ BM}$
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: (a) 1 unpaired $= 1.73\text{ BM}$, (b) 5 unpaired $= 5.92\text{ BM}$, (c) 0 unpaired $= 0\text{ BM}$, (d) 4 unpaired $= 4.90\text{ BM}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In reduction of $2,4,6$-tribromobenzenediazonium salt to $1,3,5$-tribromobenzene, reagent R is:
questions.explanation: Ethanol ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$) or hypophosphorous acid ($\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2$) reduces diazonium group $-\text{N}_2^+\text{Cl}^-$ to $-\text{H}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: From the following pairs of ions, which one is NOT an iso-electronic pair?
questions.explanation: $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ has 24 electrons ($d^6$) while $\text{Mn}^{2+}$ has 23 electrons ($d^5$).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Slope of Arrhenius plot ($\ln k$ vs $1/T$) is $-5 \times 10^3\text{ K}$. Activation energy $E_a$ is ($R = 8.314\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$):
questions.explanation: $\text{Slope} = -\frac{E_a}{R} = -5000 \implies E_a = 5000 \times 8.314 = 41.57\text{ kJ/mol}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: For irreversible isothermal expansion of an ideal gas, the correct thermodynamic conditions are:
questions.explanation: For isothermal process of ideal gas, $\Delta U = 0$. For any spontaneous irreversible process, $\Delta S_{\text{total}} > 0$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In which arrangement is the given sequence NOT strictly according to indicated property?
questions.explanation: Acidity increases down group 16 $\implies K_a$ increases $\implies pK_a$ decreases ($pK_a$ order is reversed).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In Étard reaction: $\text{Toluene} + \text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{CS}_2} X \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+} \text{PhCHO}$, intermediate $X$ is:
questions.explanation: Chromyl chloride in $\text{CS}_2$ oxidizes methyl group to brown chromium complex $\text{PhCH}(\text{OCrOHCl}_2)_2$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Vapour pressure of solution of benzene ($P^\circ = 280\text{ mm Hg}$) and octane ($P^\circ = 420\text{ mm Hg}$) in molar ratio $3:2$ is:
questions.explanation: $P_{\text{total}} = x_B P_B^\circ + x_O P_O^\circ = (0.6 \times 280) + (0.4 \times 420) = 168 + 168 = 336\text{ mm Hg}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Molar conductivity of $0.007\text{ M}$ acetic acid is $20\text{ S cm}^2\text{mol}^{-1}$ ($\Lambda^\circ_m = 400\text{ S cm}^2\text{mol}^{-1}$). Dissociation constant $K_a$ is:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In decarboxylation: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COO}^-\text{Na}^+ \xrightarrow{\text{NaOH}, ?, \Delta} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_3 + \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$, missing reagent is:
questions.explanation: Soda lime is a mixture of $\text{NaOH}$ and $\text{CaO}$ in $3:1$ ratio.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match Name Reactions:
(a) Benzene $+ \text{CO}, \text{HCl} \xrightarrow{\text{AlCl}_3/\text{CuCl}} \text{PhCHO}$, (b) $\text{RCOCH}_3 + \text{NaOX} \to \text{RCOONa} + \text{CHX}_3$, (c) $\text{RCH}_2\text{OH} + \text{R'COOH} \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+} \text{Ester}$, (d) $\text{RCH}_2\text{COOH} \xrightarrow{\text{X}_2/\text{Red P}} \alpha\text{-halo acid}$
(i) HVZ, (ii) Gattermann-Koch, (iii) Haloform, (iv) Esterification
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Gattermann-Koch = (ii), Haloform = (iii), Esterification = (iv), Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky = (i).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Reduction of ethyl 2-(3-oxocyclohexyl)acetate with $\text{NaBH}_4$ in ethanol selectively reduces:
questions.optionA: Ketone to secondary alcohol while leaving ester intact
questions.explanation: $\text{NaBH}_4$ selectively reduces aldehydes/ketones to alcohols without reducing esters.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which of the following molecules is NON-POLAR in nature?
questions.explanation: $\text{SbCl}_5$ has symmetrical trigonal bipyramidal geometry with zero net dipole moment ($\mu = 0$).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match Environmental Chemistry reactions:
(a) $2\text{SO}_2 + \text{O}_2 \to 2\text{SO}_3$, (b) $\text{HOCl} \xrightarrow{h\nu} \text{OH} + \text{Cl}$, (c) $\text{CaCO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \to \text{CaSO}_4 + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2$, (d) $\text{NO}_2 \xrightarrow{h\nu} \text{NO} + \text{O}$
(i) Acid rain, (ii) Photochemical smog, (iii) Ozone depletion, (iv) Tropospheric oxidation
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: (a) Tropospheric pollution (iv), (b) Ozone depletion (iii), (c) Acid rain (i), (d) Photochemical smog (ii).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Total pressure in $1\text{ L}$ flask at $0^\circ\text{C}$ containing $4\text{ g } \text{O}_2$ and $2\text{ g } \text{H}_2$ is ($R = 0.082\text{ L atm K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$):
questions.explanation: $n_{\text{total}} = \frac{4}{32} + \frac{2}{2} = 0.125 + 1.0 = 1.125\text{ moles}$. $P = \frac{nRT}{V} = \frac{1.125 \times 0.082 \times 273}{1} = 25.18\text{ atm}$.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following plants is MONOECIOUS?
questions.explanation: Chara is monoecious, bearing both globule (antheridium) and nucule (oogonium) on the same plant.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: A typical angiosperm embryo sac at maturity is:
questions.explanation: Polygonum type female gametophyte consists of 3 antipodals, 2 synergids, 1 egg cell, and 1 central cell with 2 polar nuclei (7 cells, 8 nuclei).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Gemmae (asexual reproductive buds) are present in:
questions.explanation: Gemmae are green, multicellular, asexual buds produced in gemma cups on thalli of liverworts like Marchantia.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: When centromere is situated in middle of two equal arms of chromosome, it is called:
questions.explanation: Metacentric chromosomes have median centromere forming two equal arms (V-shaped during anaphase).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following stages of meiosis involves division/splitting of centromeres?
questions.explanation: Centromeres split during Anaphase II of Meiosis II (analogous to mitotic anaphase), allowing sister chromatids to separate.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The first stable product of $\text{CO}_2$ fixation in sorghum ($\text{C}_4$ plant) is:
questions.explanation: In $\text{C}_4$ plants like sorghum, $\text{CO}_2$ is fixed by PEP carboxylase to form 4-carbon oxaloacetic acid.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The evolutionary factor that leads to Founder effect in a population is:
questions.explanation: Founder effect is an extreme form of genetic drift when a small founding colony establishes a new population with different allele frequencies.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following is an INCORRECT statement?
questions.optionA: Mature sieve tube elements possess a conspicuous nucleus and organelles
questions.optionB: Microbodies are present in both plant and animal cells
questions.optionC: Perinuclear space forms barrier between nucleus and cytoplasm
questions.optionD: Nuclear pores act as bidirectional passages for proteins and RNA
questions.explanation: Mature sieve tube elements lack a nucleus and depend on companion cells for metabolic functions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Amensalism population interaction is represented as:
questions.explanation: In amensalism, one species is harmed $(-)$ while other is unaffected $(0)$ (e.g. Penicillium inhibiting bacteria).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The amount of inorganic nutrients (C, N, P, Ca) present in soil at any given time is referred as:
questions.explanation: Standing state is amount of inorganic nutrients in soil; standing crop is biomass of living organisms.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following algae contains mannitol as reserve food material?
questions.explanation: Brown algae (Phaeophyceae) store complex carbohydrates as laminarin or mannitol.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: In spite of interspecific competition, competing species evolve which survival mechanism?
questions.explanation: MacArthur showed warblers avoid competition by resource partitioning (different feeding times and foraging niches).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Genera like Selaginella and Salvinia produce two kinds of spores. Such plants are:
questions.explanation: Heterosporous pteridophytes produce distinct microspores and megaspores.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The site of perception of light/dark duration in plants during photoperiodism is:
questions.explanation: Leaves perceive photoperiodic stimuli via phytochrome pigments to synthesize florigen.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Plants follow different pathways in response to environment or phases of life. This ability is:
questions.explanation: Plasticity is capacity of plants to alter morphology in response to environment (e.g. juvenile vs adult leaves in larkspur/cotton).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match List-I with List-II (Cell Organelles):
(a) Cristae, (b) Thylakoids, (c) Centromere, (d) Cisternae
(i) Primary constriction, (ii) Golgi disc-shaped sacs, (iii) Mitochondrial infoldings, (iv) Stroma membranous sacs
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Cristae = Mitochondria (iii), Thylakoids = Plastids (iv), Centromere = Chromosome (i), Cisternae = Golgi (ii).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Water Transport Properties:
(a) Cohesion, (b) Adhesion, (c) Surface tension, (d) Guttation
(i) Attraction in liquid phase, (ii) Attraction among water molecules, (iii) Water loss in liquid phase, (iv) Attraction to polar surfaces
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Cohesion = water-water (ii), Adhesion = water-tracheid wall (iv), Surface tension = liquid phase (i), Guttation = hydathode loss (iii).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: DNA strands stained with Ethidium Bromide appear under UV radiation as:
questions.explanation: EtBr intercalates in DNA base pairs and fluoresces bright orange under UV illumination.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Transfer of pollen from anther to stigma of genetically different plant is:
questions.explanation: Xenogamy brings genetically distinct pollen to stigma, promoting genetic diversity.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following algae produce the hydrocolloid Carrageen?
questions.explanation: Carrageen is extracted from red algae (e.g. Chondrus crispus).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is NOT correct about ecological pyramids?
questions.optionA: Pyramid of biomass in sea is generally inverted
questions.optionB: Pyramid of biomass in sea is generally upright
questions.optionC: Pyramid of energy is always upright
questions.optionD: Pyramid of numbers in a grassland ecosystem is upright
questions.explanation: In oceans, phytoplankton turnover is high and standing biomass of fish exceeds phytoplankton, making biomass pyramid inverted.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: In the ecological productivity equation $\text{GPP} - R = \text{NPP}$, $R$ represents:
questions.explanation: Gross Primary Productivity minus Respiratory losses ($R$) equals Net Primary Productivity ($	ext{NPP}$).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Diadelphous condition of stamens ($9 + 1$ arrangement) is found in:
questions.explanation: In Fabaceae (Pea), 10 stamens are united into two bundles: $(9) + 1$.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Gene targeting involving corrective gene insertion/amplification in patient's tissues is:
questions.explanation: Gene therapy corrects defective hereditary genes by delivering functional copies into patient tissues.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Secondary Growth Structures:
(a) Lenticels, (b) Cork cambium, (c) Secondary cortex, (d) Cork
(i) Phellogen, (ii) Suberin deposition (Phellem), (iii) Gaseous exchange, (iv) Phelloderm
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Lenticels = Gas exchange (iii), Cork cambium = Phellogen (i), Secondary cortex = Phelloderm (iv), Cork = Phellem (ii).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Production of gametes and genetic crosses ($F_1, F_2$) can be graphically understood by:
questions.explanation: British geneticist Reginald Punnett developed the Punnett square grid.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The correct sequence of steps in Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) is:
questions.explanation: Step 1: Denaturation ($94^\circ\text{C}$), Step 2: Annealing ($54^\circ\text{C}$), Step 3: Extension ($72^\circ\text{C}$ with Taq polymerase).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Mutations in plant cells for plant breeding can be artificially induced by:
questions.explanation: Ionizing radiation like Gamma rays induces chromosomal and gene mutations (e.g. mung bean resistance to yellow mosaic virus).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Biotechnology Terms:
(a) Protoplast fusion, (b) Plant tissue culture, (c) Meristem culture, (d) Micropropagation
(i) Totipotency, (ii) Pomato, (iii) Somaclones, (iv) Virus-free plants
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Protoplast fusion = Pomato (ii), Tissue culture = Totipotency (i), Meristem culture = Virus-free (iv), Micropropagation = Somaclones (iii).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: During recombinant DNA extraction, addition of chilled ethanol precipitates out:
questions.explanation: Chilled ethanol lowers DNA solubility, precipitating pure DNA fibres (spooling).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Complete Central Dogma flow chart: $\text{DNA} \xrightarrow{(a)} \text{DNA} \xrightarrow{(b)} \text{mRNA} \xrightarrow{(c)} \text{Protein} (d)$:
questions.explanation: Francis Crick proposed: DNA Replication $\to$ Transcription to mRNA $\to$ Translation to Protein.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT an application of PCR?
questions.explanation: PCR amplifies nucleic acids (DNA/RNA), not proteins.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Synthetic auxin herbicide used widely to kill broad-leaved dicot weeds is:
questions.explanation: 2,4-D selectively eradicates dicot weeds without harming mature monocot crop plants.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Plant Tissues:
(a) Actively dividing cells, (b) Similar structure and function cells, (c) Different types of cells, (d) Dead cells with thick walls and narrow lumen
(i) Vascular tissue, (ii) Meristematic tissue, (iii) Sclereids, (iv) Simple tissue
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Dividing = Meristem (ii), Uniform = Simple (iv), Complex = Vascular (i), Sclerenchyma = Sclereids (iii).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following are primary metabolites (NOT secondary metabolites)?
questions.explanation: Amino acids, sugars, and organic acids have identifiable functions in primary physiology.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following statements about respiration is INCORRECT?
questions.optionA: During aerobic respiration, role of oxygen is limited to terminal stage
questions.optionB: In ETC, $1\,\text{NADH}+\text{H}^+$ gives 2 ATP and $1\,\text{FADH}_2$ gives 3 ATP
questions.optionC: ATP is synthesized through Complex V (ATP Synthase)
questions.optionD: Redox reactions create proton gradient across inner membrane
questions.explanation: In ETC, $1\,\text{NADH}$ produces 3 ATP molecules and $1\,\text{FADH}_2$ produces 2 ATP molecules.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Nitrogen Cycle Microbes:
(a) Nitrococcus, (b) Rhizobium, (c) Thiobacillus, (d) Nitrobacter
(i) Denitrification, (ii) Ammonia to nitrite, (iii) Nitrite to nitrate, (iv) Atmospheric $\text{N}_2$ to ammonia
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Nitrococcus = $\text{NH}_3 \to \text{NO}_2^-$ (ii), Rhizobium = $\text{N}_2$ fixation (iv), Thiobacillus = Denitrification (i), Nitrobacter = $\text{NO}_2^- \to \text{NO}_3^-$ (iii).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Floral Formulas with Families:
(a) $% \,\text{K}_{(5)}\,\text{C}_{1+2+(2)}\,\text{A}_{(9)+1}\,\underline{\text{G}}_1$, (b) $\oplus \,\text{K}_{(5)}\,\widehat{\text{C}_{(5)}\,\text{A}_5}\,\underline{\text{G}}_{(2)}$, (c) $\oplus \,\widehat{\text{P}_{(3+3)}\,\text{A}_{3+3}}\,\underline{\text{G}}_{(3)}$, (d) $\oplus \,\text{K}_{2+2}\,\text{C}_4\,\text{A}_{2+4}\,\underline{\text{G}}_{(2)}$
(i) Brassicaceae, (ii) Liliaceae, (iii) Fabaceae, (iv) Solanaceae
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: (a) Fabaceae (iii), (b) Solanaceae (iv), (c) Liliaceae (ii), (d) Brassicaceae (i).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Identify the CORRECT statement regarding transcription:
questions.optionA: In capping, methylguanosine triphosphate is added to 3' end
questions.optionB: RNA polymerase binds with Rho ($\rho$) factor to terminate transcription in bacteria
questions.optionC: The coding strand is transcribed into mRNA
questions.optionD: Split gene arrangement is characteristic of prokaryotes
questions.explanation: Rho factor binds to RNA polymerase to terminate bacterial transcription.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is CORRECT?
questions.optionA: Fusion of two cells is karyogamy
questions.optionB: Fusion of protoplasms between two gametes is called plasmogamy
questions.optionC: Organisms depending on living plants are saprophytes
questions.optionD: Nitrogen fixation occurs in sheath cells
questions.explanation: Plasmogamy is the fusion of vegetative/gametic protoplasm prior to karyogamy.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Select the CORRECT anatomical pair:
questions.optionA: Large colourless empty cells in grass epidermis - Subsidiary cells
questions.optionB: Vascular bundle sheath in dicots - Conjunctive tissue
questions.optionC: Medullary ray cells forming cambial ring - Interfascicular cambium
questions.optionD: Loose cells forming lenticels - Spongy parenchyma
questions.explanation: Cells of medullary rays adjoining intrafascicular cambium dedifferentiate into interfascicular cambium.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: DNA fingerprinting involves identifying differences in specific non-coding regions called:
questions.explanation: DNA fingerprinting detects variations in tandem repetitive DNA sequences (VNTRs/mini-satellites).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: In members of which families do pollen grains retain viability for several months?
questions.explanation: Cereals (Poaceae) lose pollen viability in 30 minutes; Rosaceae, Leguminosae, and Solanaceae retain viability for months.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following statements about photosynthesis is INCORRECT?
questions.optionA: Both ATP and NADPH are synthesized during non-cyclic photophosphorylation
questions.optionB: Stroma lamellae possess PS I only and lack NADP reductase
questions.optionC: Grana lamellae possess both PS I and PS II
questions.optionD: Cyclic photophosphorylation involves both PS I and PS II
questions.explanation: Cyclic photophosphorylation involves only Photosystem I (PS I).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Role of RNA polymerase III in eukaryotic transcription is to synthesize:
questions.explanation: RNA Pol I transcribes 28S, 18S, 5.8S rRNAs; RNA Pol II transcribes hnRNA; RNA Pol III transcribes tRNA, 5S rRNA, and snRNAs.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: In the exponential population growth equation $N_t = N_0 e^{rt}$, '$e$' represents:
questions.explanation: In continuous growth models, $e$ is base of natural logarithm ($e \approx 2.718$).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: A mutated cancer gene does NOT appear on photographic film during autoradiography because:
questions.optionC: Mutated gene does not bind the radioactive probe due to lack of base complementarity
questions.explanation: Single-stranded radiolabeled probe fails to hybridize with the mutated sequence, leaving no signal on autoradiogram.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Biomolecules with Chemical Bonds:
(a) Protein, (b) Unsaturated fatty acid, (c) Nucleic acid, (d) Polysaccharide
(i) $\text{C}=\text{C}$ double bonds, (ii) Phosphodiester bonds, (iii) Glycosidic bonds, (iv) Peptide bonds
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Protein = Peptide (iv), Unsaturated lipid = C=C (i), Nucleic acid = Phosphodiester (ii), Polysaccharide = Glycosidic (iii).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Cell Cycle Stages:
(a) S phase, (b) G2 phase, (c) Quiescent ($G_0$), (d) G1 phase
(i) Protein synthesis, (ii) Metabolically active inactive-division stage, (iii) Interval between mitosis and replication, (iv) DNA replication
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: S = DNA synthesis (iv), G2 = Tubulin/protein synthesis (i), G0 = Quiescent state (ii), G1 = Post-mitotic gap (iii).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Inserting $\beta$-galactosidase gene into PstI site of $amp^R$ in pBR322 leads to:
questions.optionA: Insertional inactivation: host cells lose ampicillin resistance
questions.optionB: Transformed cells resist ampicillin and produce $\beta$-galactosidase
questions.explanation: Disruption of $amp^R$ coding sequence by foreign insert destroys ampicillin resistance (insertional inactivation).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Identify the INCORRECT secondary metabolite pair:
questions.optionD: Drugs - Ricin (Ricin is a toxin, not drug)
questions.explanation: Ricin and Abrin are poisonous toxins; Vinblastin and Curcumin are drugs.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Fruit fly has 8 chromosomes ($2n=8$). If chromosome number at $G_1$ is 8, chromosome number after S phase is:
questions.explanation: During S phase, DNA content doubles ($2C \to 4C$) but chromosome number remains identical ($2n = 8$).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Animal Kingdom Features:
(a) Metamerism, (b) Water canal system, (c) Comb plates, (d) Cnidoblasts
(i) Coelenterata, (ii) Ctenophora, (iii) Annelida, (iv) Porifera
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Metamerism = Annelida (iii), Canal system = Sponges (iv), Ciliated plates = Ctenophora (ii), Cnidocytes = Coelenterates (i).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Contraceptive Methods:
(a) Vaults, (b) IUDs, (c) Vasectomy, (d) Tubectomy
(i) Block sperm entry at cervix, (ii) Cut/ligate vas deferens, (iii) Phagocytosis of sperms in uterus, (iv) Cut/ligate fallopian tube
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Vaults = Cervical barrier (i), IUDs = Phagocytosis (iii), Vasectomy = Vas deferens (ii), Tubectomy = Fallopian tube (iv).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: If Adenine makes $30\%$ of DNA bases, percentages of T, G, and C are:
questions.explanation: Chargaff's rules: $\%A = \%T = 30\%$. Remaining $40\%$ is split equally: $\%G = \%C = 20\%$.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following RNAs is NOT required for mRNA translation into protein?
questions.optionD: siRNA (involved in RNA interference, not translation)
questions.explanation: Translation machinery uses mRNA, tRNA, and rRNA; siRNA is an RNA silencing agent.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following is a hormone-releasing intrauterine device (IUD)?
questions.explanation: LNG-20 and Progestasert are hormone-releasing IUDs.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Succus entericus is another name for:
questions.explanation: Secretions of crypts of Lieberkühn and Brunner's glands constitute intestinal juice (succus entericus).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Chronic autoimmune disorder affecting neuromuscular junction causing muscle weakness and paralysis is:
questions.explanation: Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disease where autoantibodies block acetylcholine receptors at neuromuscular junctions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Choose correct statements regarding human insulin:
(a) C-peptide is absent in mature insulin
(b) rDNA insulin contains C-peptide
(c) Pro-insulin contains C-peptide
(d) A and B chains are connected by disulfide bridges
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Statements (a), (c), (d) are true. Humulin produced by rDNA lacks C-peptide.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following insects belongs to the family Muscidae?
questions.explanation: Housefly (Musca domestica) belongs to Order Diptera, Family Muscidae.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The single enzyme capable of initiating, elongating and terminating transcription in prokaryotes is:
questions.explanation: Bacterial RNA polymerase holoenzyme associates with $\sigma$ factor for initiation and $\rho$ factor for termination.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Primary glycoprotein receptors (ZP3) for sperm binding in mammalian fertilization are on:
questions.explanation: Capacitated sperm binds to ZP3 receptors on the zona pellucida, inducing acrosome reaction.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Centriole duplication in animal cells occurs during which cell cycle phase?
questions.explanation: While DNA replicates in the nucleus during S-phase, centrioles duplicate in the cytoplasm.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which organism possesses hollow pneumatic bones to reduce weight for flight?
questions.explanation: Birds (Neophron) possess air-filled pneumatic long bones for flight adaptation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Erythropoietin (EPO) hormone that stimulates erythropoiesis is secreted by:
questions.explanation: Renal JG cells release erythropoietin in response to hypoxia.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Animals with Common Names:
(a) Physalia, (b) Limulus, (c) Ancylostoma, (d) Pinctada
(i) Pearl oyster, (ii) Portuguese Man-of-War, (iii) Living fossil king crab, (iv) Hookworm
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Physalia = Portuguese Man-of-War (ii), Limulus = Living fossil (iii), Ancylostoma = Hookworm (iv), Pinctada = Pearl oyster (i).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: If high temperature ($94^\circ\text{C}$) is not maintained initially in PCR, which step is affected first?
questions.explanation: High temperature disrupts hydrogen bonds to separate template double helix during denaturation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which statement WRONGLY represents smooth muscle tissue?
questions.optionC: Intercellular communication occurs via intercalated discs (Intercalated discs are in cardiac muscle)
questions.optionD: They are present in walls of blood vessels and hollow organs
questions.explanation: Intercalated discs with gap junctions are unique to cardiac muscle.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Organelles included in the endomembrane system are:
questions.optionB: Endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus, Lysosomes, and Vacuoles
questions.explanation: The endomembrane system consists of coordinated ER, Golgi complex, Lysosomes, and Vacuoles.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Microbes with Organic Acids:
(a) Aspergillus niger, (b) Acetobacter aceti, (c) Clostridium butylicum, (d) Lactobacillus
(i) Acetic acid, (ii) Lactic acid, (iii) Citric acid, (iv) Butyric acid
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Aspergillus = Citric (iii), Acetobacter = Acetic (i), Clostridium = Butyric (iv), Lactobacillus = Lactic (ii).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which molecular diagnostic technique is widely used for early detection of HIV/antigens?
questions.explanation: ELISA detects low titers of viral antigens or antibodies based on antigen-antibody interactions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which characteristic is INCORRECT with respect to Cockroach (Periplaneta americana)?
questions.optionA: Ring of 6-8 hepatic caeca is present at junction of foregut and midgut (NOT midgut and hindgut)
questions.optionB: Hypopharynx acts as tongue within mouthparts cavity
questions.optionC: In females, 7th-9th sterna form brood/genital pouch
questions.optionD: 10th abdominal segment in both sexes bears anal cerci
questions.explanation: Gastric/hepatic caeca are at the gizzard-midgut junction; Malpighian tubules are at midgut-hindgut junction.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Persons with AB blood group are universal recipients due to:
questions.optionA: Absence of antigens A and B on RBCs
questions.optionB: Absence of antigens A and B in plasma
questions.optionC: Presence of antibodies anti-A and anti-B on RBCs
questions.optionD: Absence of antibodies anti-A and anti-B in plasma
questions.explanation: AB individuals possess both A and B antigens on RBCs and lack anti-A and anti-B antibodies in plasma.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Dobson Units (DU) are standard units used to measure the thickness of:
questions.explanation: Ozone column thickness is measured in Dobson Units ($1\text{ DU} = 0.01\text{ mm}$ at STP).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Choose the correct statements regarding animal phyla:
(a) Metagenesis in Helminths
(b) Echinoderms are triploblastic and coelomate
(c) Roundworms have organ-system level organization
(d) Comb plates help in digestion
(e) Water vascular system in Echinoderms
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Metagenesis occurs in Cnidarians (Obelia). Comb plates are for locomotion. Statements (b), (c), (e) are correct.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: In a cross between two carriers ($Hb^A Hb^S$) for sickle cell anaemia, percentage of diseased progeny ($Hb^S Hb^S$) is:
questions.explanation: $Hb^A Hb^S \times Hb^A Hb^S \to 1\,Hb^A Hb^A : 2\,Hb^A Hb^S : 1\,Hb^S Hb^S \implies 25\%$ affected.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which enzyme catalyzes conversion of inactive soluble fibrinogen to insoluble fibrin threads in blood clotting?
questions.explanation: Thrombin converts fibrinogen to fibrin monomers that polymerize to form the clot.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Favourable physiological conditions for oxyhaemoglobin formation in lung alveoli are:
questions.optionA: High $pO_2$, low $pCO_2$, low $H^+$ (higher pH), and lower temperature
questions.explanation: High $pO_2$, low $pCO_2$, low acidity ($H^+$), and lower temperature shift the oxygen dissociation curve to the left, favoring binding.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Sphincter of Oddi guards the opening of:
questions.optionB: Junction of common hepato-pancreatic duct into duodenum
questions.explanation: Hepato-pancreatic ampulla opens into the descending duodenum guarded by the Sphincter of Oddi.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which stage of prophase I of meiosis is marked by terminalisation of chiasmata?
questions.explanation: Final stage of prophase I is Diakinesis, characterized by complete terminalisation of chiasmata and nuclear envelope breakdown.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a primary breeding objective of Biofortification?
questions.explanation: Biofortification focuses specifically on nutritional enrichment (vitamins, proteins, micronutrients), not disease resistance.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Partial pressures (in mm Hg) of oxygen ($pO_2$) and carbon dioxide ($pCO_2$) in alveolar air are:
questions.explanation: Alveolar gas composition: $pO_2 = 104\text{ mm Hg}$ and $pCO_2 = 40\text{ mm Hg}$.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Venereal diseases (STDs like Hepatitis-B and HIV) can spread through:
(a) Sterile needles
(b) Transfusion of infected blood
(c) Infected mother to fetus
(d) Kissing
(e) Genetic inheritance
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Blood transfusion from infected donor and vertical transmission from mother to fetus transmit Hepatitis-B and HIV.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Specific symmetrical DNA recognition sequences cleaved by restriction endonucleases are:
questions.explanation: Restriction enzymes recognize 4-8 bp palindromic sequences reading identical in $5' \to 3'$ direction on both strands.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which statement about basic Histone proteins is WRONG?
questions.optionA: Histones organize into an octamer core of 8 molecules
questions.optionB: The pH of histones is slightly acidic
questions.optionC: Histones are rich in basic amino acids Lysine and Arginine
questions.optionD: Histones carry positive charges on basic side chains
questions.explanation: Histones are basic proteins with alkaline pH due to positively charged basic amino acids.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
During skeletal muscle contraction, which events occur?
(a) H-zone disappears
(b) A-band widens
(c) I-band shortens
(d) Myosin hydrolyzes ATP
(e) Z-lines are pulled inward
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: A-band length remains constant during contraction (statement b is false).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Skeletal System Bones:
(a) Scapula, (b) Cranium, (c) Sternum, (d) Vertebral column
(i) Cartilaginous joints, (ii) Flat bone, (iii) Fibrous/sutural joints, (iv) Triangular flat bone
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Scapula = Triangular flat bone (iv), Cranium = Fibrous sutures (iii), Sternum = Flat bone (ii), Vertebrae = Cartilaginous joints (i).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which hormone is NOT directly involved in the initiation of parturition in humans?
questions.optionD: Prolactin release (responsible for lactation/milk secretion post-birth)
questions.explanation: Prolactin stimulates milk synthesis post-partum, not fetal expulsion/parturition.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Assertion (A): High altitude sickness causes breathlessness and heart palpitations.
Reason (R): Low atmospheric pressure decreases oxygen binding to haemoglobin.
Choose correct option:
questions.optionA: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is correct explanation of (A)
questions.optionB: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: At high altitudes, lower ambient $pO_2$ causes hypoxia, triggering compensatory hyperventilation and tachycardia.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Choose the correct statements regarding lipids:
(a) Lipids with only single bonds are unsaturated
(b) Lecithin is a phospholipid
(c) Trihydroxypropane is glycerol
(d) Palmitic acid has 20 carbons
(e) Arachidonic acid has 16 carbons
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Lecithin is a phospholipid (b); Glycerol is propane-1,2,3-triol (c). Palmitic acid has 16 carbons; arachidonic has 20.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency causes:
questions.explanation: ADA deficiency causes toxic accumulation of dATP, destroying B and T lymphocytes and causing SCID.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: The hormone Relaxin is secreted during the later phase of pregnancy by:
questions.explanation: Corpus luteum of ovary (and placenta) secretes relaxin to soften pelvic ligaments for childbirth.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Junctions that stop substance leakage and facilitate rapid ion/metabolite communication are:
questions.optionB: Tight junctions and Gap junctions, respectively
questions.explanation: Tight junctions prevent extracellular leakage; Gap junctions permit rapid intercellular ionic communication.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText: Which is NOT a step in Multiple Ovulation Embryo Transfer (MOET)?
questions.optionA: Cow is administered hormone with LH-like activity (FSH-like activity is administered)
questions.optionD: Embryos are recovered non-surgically at 8-32 cell stage into surrogates
questions.explanation: FSH-like hormones are administered to induce superovulation (not LH).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Pathogens with Diseases:
(a) Filariasis, (b) Amoebiasis, (c) Pneumonia, (d) Ringworm
(i) Haemophilus influenzae, (ii) Trichophyton, (iii) Wuchereria bancrofti, (iv) Entamoeba histolytica
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Filariasis = Wuchereria (iii), Amoebiasis = Entamoeba (iv), Pneumonia = Haemophilus (i), Ringworm = Trichophyton (ii).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Adaptations:
(a) Allen's Rule, (b) Physiological adaptation, (c) Behavioural adaptation, (d) Biochemical adaptation
(i) Kangaroo rat, (ii) Desert lizard, (iii) Marine fish at high pressure, (iv) Polar seal (blubber / short extremities)
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Allen's Rule = Polar seal (iv), Physiological = Kangaroo rat water conservation (i), Behavioural = Desert lizard basking (ii), Biochemical = Deep-sea barophiles (iii).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Match Evolutionary Patterns:
(a) Adaptive radiation, (b) Convergent evolution, (c) Divergent evolution, (d) Anthropogenic action
(i) Herbicide/pesticide resistance, (ii) Forelimbs of Man and Whale, (iii) Wings of Butterfly and Bird, (iv) Darwin’s Finches
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Adaptive radiation = Galapagos finches (iv), Convergent = Wings of butterfly & bird (iii), Divergent = Mammalian forelimbs (ii), Anthropogenic = Pesticide resistance (i).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Statement I: Codon 'AUG' codes for methionine and phenylalanine.
Statement II: 'AAA' and 'AAG' both code for lysine.
Choose correct option:
questions.optionA: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
questions.optionB: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.optionC: Statement I is correct but Statement II is false
questions.optionD: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true
questions.explanation: AUG codes exclusively for Methionine (initiator codon), not phenylalanine (Statement I false). AAA and AAG code for Lysine (Statement II true).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.questionText:
Which statements are correct about prostomium of Earthworm (Pheretima)?
(a) Serves as wedge covering mouth
(b) Helps open cracks in soil for burrowing
(c) Acts as a sensory structure
(d) It is the first body segment (Peristomium is first segment)
Choose correct option:
questions.explanation: Prostomium is an anterior sensory lobe overhang (not a body segment); peristomium (buccal segment) is the first segment.
